# Review — PR #389 (issue #374), iteration 5, head 8b0c62d

## Verdict

REJECT — one Critical checklist item fails (VC-174, criterion 20).

## Critical

- VC-174: FAIL (critical) — Under the example set, a statement the rule-set guard cannot carry through is refused before execution, with no SQL reaching MySQL, at minimum in these cases: a `run_sql` argument whose parse yields no statement (empty text and comment-only text), and an exception raised in each of the guard's parse, analyze, rewrite and generate steps, including an exception type the guard does not name. Each refusal's client-facing text begins with `Refused by the rule set:` and names no table, column or function. [src/sqllens/agent/factory.py:127-140] — fix the code, or have the issue author amend this criterion

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  Graded with criteria.json (criterion 20 present). Guard-internal behavior conforms: rule_sets.py:108-129 _parse refuses empty text (readonly._parse_statements raises 'empty SQL', mapped to KIND_UNPARSEABLE) and comment-only text (None statement -> KIND_NOT_ONE_SELECT); RuleSetGuardRunner.run_sql (rule_sets.py:358-375) catches RuleSetRefusal and bare Exception around _parse/_analyze/_rewrite/_generate/_reparse and raises RuleSetRefusal(KIND_UNCHECKED) with the 'Refused by the rule set: ' prefix before the inner runner is called; unit test test_any_exception_in_a_step_refuses_with_no_sql_passed_on covers each step. DEPARTURE: in the shipped composition (agent/factory.py:132-140) WholeRowSelectGuardRunner (default refuse_whole_row_selects=True, config.py:77-78) sits OUTSIDE RuleSetGuardRunner and runs first. For empty text, _whole_row_reference -> _parse_statements raises UnsafeSqlError('empty SQL') (readonly.py:539-540); for comment-only text it raises UnsafeSqlError('empty parse tree') (whole_row.py:122-123). whole_row.py:217-218 re-raises it as UnsafeSqlError, the rule-set guard is never reached, and RefusalRedactingRunner.redacted_refusal_text (rule_sets.py:420-421, markers 'empty SQL'/'empty parse tree') turns it into REDACTED_PARSE = 'refusing to execute SQL: could not parse SQL', which does not begin with 'Refused by the rule set:'. Criterion 20 requires that prefix on each refusal for these cases under the example set; sibling criterion 25 only requires the prefix on 'rule-set guard' refusals and does not name whole-row-guard refusals of empty or comment-only text, so it does not excuse this. Tests only exercise the guard runner alone (test_safety_rule_sets.py:223-224, 376-396) and no end-to-end test covers empty or comment-only text through the full runner stack.

  </details>

### 1. Empty and comment-only `run_sql` text is refused by the whole-row guard, not the rule-set guard, so its client text lacks the `Refused by the rule set:` prefix criterion 20 requires

Criterion 20 names two cases by hand — "a `run_sql` argument whose parse
yields no statement (empty text and comment-only text)" — and requires that
"Each refusal's client-facing text begins with `Refused by the rule set:`".

In the shipped composition (`src/sqllens/agent/factory.py` lines 132-140)
`WholeRowSelectGuardRunner` is wrapped *outside* `RuleSetGuardRunner` and runs
first. For empty text its `_parse_statements` call raises
`UnsafeSqlError("empty SQL")`; for comment-only text `_whole_row_reference`
raises `UnsafeSqlError("empty parse tree")`
(`src/sqllens/safety/whole_row.py` lines 120-123, re-raised at lines 217-218).
The rule-set guard is never reached, and `RefusalRedactingRunner` maps both
markers to `REDACTED_PARSE` — "refusing to execute SQL: could not parse SQL" —
which does not carry the required prefix.

The guard itself is correct in isolation: called directly it refuses both cases
(`KIND_UNPARSEABLE` / `KIND_NOT_ONE_SELECT`) with the prefix, and
`tests/unit/test_safety_rule_sets.py` covers that. The gap is that no test
exercises empty or comment-only text through the composed runner stack, which
is the configuration criterion 20 describes.

Criterion 25 does not excuse this: it requires only that whole-row-guard
refusals name no identifier (they do not) and that *rule-set guard* refusals
carry the prefix.

Resolving this means deciding which component owns the refusal text for
unparseable input while a rule-set file is configured — reorder the two guards,
or widen the redactor's parse arm to carry the rule-set prefix. Both change
behaviour the issue does not settle, and both change text and ordering that
existing tests and the internal docs pin.

## Suggestions

- VC-71: FAIL (suggestion) — The runner docstring asserts the whole-row guard is composed beneath ResultMaskingRunner (and, with a rule-set file, RefusalRedactingRunner) and outside every runner that rewrites or runs SQL, naming RlsGuardRunner, ReadOnlyGuardRunner, RowCapRunner and the engine runner. [src/sqllens/safety/whole_row.py:197]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  factory.py:111-148 composes (inner to outer): engine runner (build_sql_runner), RowCapRunner (118), ReadOnlyGuardRunner (121), RlsGuardRunner (128), RuleSetGuardRunner (132, only with a rule-set file), WholeRowSelectGuardRunner (137), RefusalRedactingRunner (140), ResultMaskingRunner (143). So the guard is beneath masking and refusal redaction and outside the four named runners, as the docstring says. But the docstring's parenthetical enumerates the runners that rewrite or run SQL and omits RuleSetGuardRunner, which also sits inside the whole-row guard and rewrites SQL (rule_sets.py:320-343, _rewrite builds derived tables). With a rule-set file, the very configuration the docstring mentions, the list is incomplete, and the 'before any row-level-security rewrite' framing leaves out the rule-set rewrite. Authored docstring drift: the 'every runner' statement is true, but its named list is not exhaustive.

  </details>

### 1. `WholeRowSelectGuardRunner`'s docstring omits `RuleSetGuardRunner` from the runners it wraps

`src/sqllens/safety/whole_row.py` lines 197-201 say the guard is composed
"outside every runner that rewrites or runs SQL (`RlsGuardRunner`,
`ReadOnlyGuardRunner`, `RowCapRunner` and the engine runner), so it checks the
SQL the agent wrote, before any row-level-security rewrite." With a rule-set
file, `RuleSetGuardRunner` also sits inside it and also rewrites SQL
(`src/sqllens/safety/rule_sets.py` lines 320-343 build the derived tables), so
the parenthetical list is incomplete and the "before any row-level-security
rewrite" framing omits the rule-set rewrite.

### 2. The `_request_metadata` docstring says the declared-key count replaces the extras count; both apply

`src/sqllens/server.py` lines 206-209 read "With `count_declared_keys` the
limit *instead* counts every key the caller sent in `_meta`", but the check
keeps both bounds (`len(extra) > 64 or len(sent) > 64`). The sibling prose in
`docs/internal/database-connectors/row-level-security.md` line 281 was
corrected in this change to "a second key limit applies beside it", so the two
surfaces now disagree.

### 3. `docs/external/rule-sets.md` line 66 contradicts line 99 on `confirmed_against_production`

Line 66 says `confirmed_against_production = true` "is required"; only the key
is required (`Source.confirmed_against_production: StrictBool`). A set carrying
`false` loads and draws the `Warning:` line 99 describes, then is refused at
selection time.

### 4. `docs/internal/database-connectors/rule-sets.md` line 64 misstates the redacted text for the `RlsError` family

The page says a refusal recognised by `_logged_by_guard` "is redacted to
`REDACTED_GUARD_ERROR` (`KIND_UNCHECKED`) rather than to a statement-refusal
kind". `redacted_refusal_text` (`src/sqllens/safety/rule_sets.py` lines
412-419) returns a statement-refusal kind for every `RlsError` *before*
`_logged_by_guard` is consulted at line 422, so `RlsGuardRunner`'s fail-closed
refusal reaches the model as `REDACTED_RLS` and the relation check's as
`REDACTED_RELATION`, never `REDACTED_GUARD_ERROR`. Only the
`UnsafeSqlError`-family guards behave as described. No name leaks either way.

### 5. Freshness markers on the internal pages this change edits predate the edits

`docs/internal/database-connectors/rule-sets.md` line 3 records
`verified-against: 97783a1`, two commits behind this head. The pages whose
content this change modifies also keep older markers:
`read-only-safety.md` and `row-level-security.md` (`eff9038`),
`agent/factory.md`, `setup/preflight.md` and `setup/config-loading.md`
(`caaa838`), `mcp-server/tools.md` (`0fbeec6`).

### 6. `_check_catalog_blocking` duplicates the preflight connect timeout as a literal

`src/sqllens/rule_sets.py` line 243 hard-codes `connect_timeout=5`, repeating
`preflight._DB_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` on the sibling request-time path. The
two bounds drift silently if the constant is tuned, and this is the path where
an unreachable database makes every refused request wait the full timeout
inside the conversation-turn lock.

### 7. The guard's detail for comment-only text reports a count that is not the reason

`src/sqllens/safety/rule_sets.py` lines 113-116: comment-only or
whitespace-only text parses to a single `None` element, so the guard takes the
`statements[0] is None` branch but logs `"expected one statement, got 1"`. The
client-facing kind is right; the operator-facing detail — the only diagnostic
for that refusal — states a count that does not explain it.

### 8. `_RuleSetUserResolver` cannot express "no identity"

`src/sqllens/agent/factory.py` lines 70-84: when `current_rule_set_selection()`
returns `None` while a rule-set file is configured, the resolver falls back to
`_StaticUserResolver`'s shared `DEFAULT_USER_ID` with no log record, while
every other rule-set component treats a missing selection as an error
(`RuleSetGuardRunner._rewrite` raises `KIND_NO_SELECTION`). Any path reaching
the agent without publishing a selection gets an identity that collides with
every other such request instead of a refusal.

### 9. The conversation-owner lookup is a runtime attribute probe

`src/sqllens/tools/query_database.py` lines 229-245 use
`getattr(agent.conversation_store, "owner_id", None)` plus a hand-raised
`TypeError` in place of a method the `ConversationStore` protocol does not
declare. Another store satisfying the declared protocol type-checks but makes
every rule-set request with a conversation ID fail closed at runtime. The path
fails closed today, so this is correctness-preserving but unexpressed.

### 10. `TableRule.row_rule` is an `Any` field used only for presence detection

`src/sqllens/rule_sets.py` lines 174-178: the field accepts any value at schema
level and the "row rules are not supported" rule is enforced afterwards by
inspecting `model_fields_set`. A `TableRule` built in Python with an explicit
`row_rule=None` is rejected even though that is the default, and the type says
nothing about what a version-2 `row_rule` will be.

## Checked and found sound

- The guard was exercised directly against ~40 statements drawn from criteria
  11, 12, 16, 17, 18, 20, 21 and 25: derived-table wrapping, parenthesized
  joins, LATERAL bodies, CTE references, and the refusals for catalog schemas,
  qualified tables, `DUAL`, `JSON_TABLE`, `PARTITION`, index hints,
  `SELECT … INTO`, `TABLE t`, executable comments, optimizer-hint breakout and
  unparseable text all behave as the criteria require.
- Ordering: selection runs before the profile lookup; the owner check and
  `ensure_catalog_confirmed` run inside the turn lock; the rule-set guard sits
  outside flat RLS; the redactor sits outside every guard; the `sql_mode` step
  raises before any query runs.
- The single-WARNING-per-refusal rule (criterion 26) holds on every traced
  path, including both `RlsGuardRunner` re-raise shapes.
- `sqlglot` 30.22 and 30.31 both name the `Select` argument `from_`, so
  `_is_guard_derived` is correct across the allowed range.
